long_biography.plain_text:
Roger Samuelsson reached Taiwan by following the supply chain of his boxing equipment. While studying engineering in Sweden, he noticed where his gloves were made, visited the island and began exporting local products. He later settled there and co-founded the trading business that became SHL Medical. A contract to build injectors for Upjohn redirected the company towards drug delivery.

Samuelsson then concentrated on autoinjectors and invested early in machinery that could automate production. Combining device design with in-house manufacturing enabled SHL to scale self-injection systems. He handed executive leadership to Ulrich Fässler but kept a majority stake, preserving founder ownership after withdrawing from day-to-day operations.

Samuelsson then concentrated on autoinjectors and invested early in machinery that could automate production. He handed executive leadership to Ulrich Fässler but kept a majority stake, preserving founder ownership after withdrawing from day-to-day operations.
